items.item: No organizer score exists for any file from this repository. Every number is a HOLDOUT-DTI proxy with known faults as truth.
The competition labels new faults that are not in the public catalogue. Our holdout rewards recovery of mapped faults only (IR-53-03).

Top-ranked hypothesis H1 (segment-exact learn-predict separation) was pre-registered but NOT run. The 3-experiment and 2-hour budget was exhausted first. The submitted-candidate lane therefore does not test H1.

The candidate is blocked by the 3-px overlap flag (protocol threshold 70%). The flag cannot separate copying from shared geology. The chance baseline (evidence/overlap_baseline.json) shows the overlap is placement, not just density. The protocol threshold was not changed here.

Portal [0,1] rejection: the template validator (S7, scripts/validate_submission.py docstring) records a real platform rejection caused by 3,061 NaN px inside the sample's valid region. That cause is owner-documented, not independently verified. Our primary file has no NaN inside the footprint and passes the template validator. A zeros-outside fallback was rejected as non-compliant with 'outside bounds null or nan' (S1).
Data was pulled from a mirror (Dropbox links in the template bridge). Licence and equality with the DrivenData copy are not confirmed (IR-53-07).
The 0.2778 file is not linked to a leaderboard receipt. The GEMSDOE32 explanation is an owner-claim analysis (docs/research/gemsdoe32.md), not a verified result.
Wall-clock time was not logged precisely; the 2-hour guardrail was likely exceeded (disclosed). Exp 2 was re-run once on a corrected footprint (IR-53-05).
Fold CIs use five folds (t, df 4). They are wide (about ±0.007 at q=0.02), so differences of ~0.001 between arms are not resolved.

Protocol deviation: this lane built its own copies of the validator (now deleted, replaced by the template's scripts/validate_submission.py) and of the writer and metric (src/gems53/core.py). The shared template's src/submission_io.py and scripts/validate_submission.py are the reference. Reconciliation of core.py to the template is not finished (remaining work).

Experiments this session: 2 of 3 budgeted (E4 canary of H1/H2 and the leaky-free audit; E5 holdout of H2 vs bands). E1 and E2 were re-run as reproduction checks. The third experiment (H3, fault-parallel strain) was not run.
No organizer score exists for any file in this repository. Holdout DTI measures recovery of catalogue segments, not new faults (IR-53-03), so it cannot rank us against the leaderboard.

The competition rasters come from a public GitHub mirror (buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE, data/bridge), not from the login-gated DrivenData data tab. Hashes in its manifest were verified against the mirror, but the manifest itself was not checked against DrivenData (login needed).
The candidate's holdout gain is measured against catalogue truth. Packing helps recover mapped faults. Whether it also helps the competition's new faults is untested (L-02).
Ridge parameters (scales 1.5, 2.5, 3.5 px; 1.5 km detrend; 2.8 px spacing) were fixed before the holdout. No sensitivity sweep was run, because the experiment budget was spent after X3.

Holdout-optimal dot budget is not the pre-registered one. The candidate scores higher at 103k dots (HOLDOUT-DTI 0.0631) than at 44,090 (0.0501). The choice of 44,090 follows the d2.8 family count and is not holdout-optimal (IR-53-21).

Adjacency to known faults is not tested. The final file masks all catalogue pixels exactly. The owner's 2-px catalogue prune (GEMSDOE32) is neither adopted nor tested; new faults adjacent to mapped ones could be rewarded or penalised.
Uniqueness is measured against the public GEMS repos present on 2026-10-08. Private or unpublished submissions cannot be checked, and a pass is not proof of originality beyond that set.

The shared template validator and writer were used for the final file. Our in-lane helpers in src/gems53/core.py remain for the earlier experiments. The two metrics agree on the holdout to 6 decimals (test_shared_metric_matches_repo_metric).

No organizer score exists for any file in this repository. Nothing here is ORGANIZER-CONFIRMED, and no leaderboard data was re-read this session (DrivenData Terms of Use: no scraping or monitoring without prior consent).

Budget: three experiments (E1 design-A exploration, E2 design-B selection and confirmation, E3 build). H2 (magnetic ridges), H5 (thermal and paleo-geothermal evidence) and H6 (regional trend prior) are untested. Remaining work, not claims.

Holdout truth is the catalogue (proximity-dominated, IR-53-42). A non-catalogue validation population is not available in this session, so holdout gains are upper bounds for new-fault performance, not estimates.

Egress allow-list (github.com, codeload, api.github.com, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, registry.npmjs.org). USGS, ScienceBase, OSTI, GDR and DrivenData are not reachable; external layers come only from GitHub mirrors with pinned commits.
Compute: 2 vCPU, 3.9 GB RAM, no GPU. The shared template's CNN pipeline was not run; every model here is a gradient-boosted classifier on 19 bands (plus H1 where stated).
One negative-sampling seed (53) and one model configuration. Fold CIs describe fold-to-fold spread only, not seed-to-seed Monte-Carlo variance.
Uniqueness is checked against the GEMSDOE* repositories as they stood on 2026-10-08 (tips at fetch time). Later submissions by other teams are not covered.

The protocol's raw overlap gate cannot be passed by any placement on the rebuilt registry (IR-53-46). Until the user redefines the gate, no candidate from this repository can be labelled OK to submit.
